summary_html: Agency or court authorizes **immediate medical or psychological care** when delay endangers life or safety. Federal statutes support medical access and confidentiality exceptions for child protection.
authority_html:
- **CAPTA (42 U.S.C. §§ 5101–5116)** — permits emergency medical actions for abused/neglected children  
- **Victims of Child Abuse Act (34 U.S.C. §§ 20301–20307)** — multidisciplinary response and medical-exam standards

key_cases.holding: The court affirmed the order keeping a seventeen year old in DCF custody for chemotherapy, holding the trial court's finding that she was not a mature minor competent to make her own medical decisions was not clearly erroneous, and declining on this record to adopt the mature minor doctrine.
key_cases.relevance: This is Connecticut's leading decision authorizing state-compelled life-saving medical treatment of a child over the objection of the child and parent.
key_cases.quote: her finding that Cassandra was not a mature minor was not clearly erroneous

timeline_requirements.starts_from: Issuance of the ex parte order of temporary custody or order to appear

notice_requirements.timing: At the commencement of any proceeding on behalf of a neglected, uncared-for or abused child or youth, and again at the preliminary hearing on an order of temporary custody or order to appear
content_required: The parent or guardian has the right to counsel and must be so informed by the judge
If the parent or guardian is unable to afford counsel, counsel will be provided
The parent or guardian has the rights of confrontation and cross-examination

The court may also appoint counsel for the parent or guardian without a request if it determines the interests of justice so require (Conn. Gen. Stat. § 46b-136(a)); in a proceeding in which the custody of a child is at issue the judge must provide an attorney for the child

Cost of appointed counsel in the civil juvenile session is shared as agreed by the Division of Public Defender Services and the Judicial Department, and the court may order a party found able to pay to reimburse that cost (Conn. Gen. Stat. § 46b-136(b)(1))
notice_requirements.defective_notice_consequence: Not specified in Conn. Gen. Stat. §§ 46b-135 or 46b-136

statutory_basis.citation_text: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 46b-135(b) (right to counsel and cross-examination); see also § 46b-136 (appointment of attorney; payment) and § 46b-129(c)(1) (advisement at the preliminary hearing)
